goldenComparison.justification: The initial DirectX11/DXVK campaign requires two independent production-viewer processes to produce byte-identical PNG files before any renderer-owned golden is accepted. The renderer has its own golden set; no EasyGL, Vulkan or SOFTWARE image or tolerance is reused.

classification.scope: Differences between this run and the committed same-renderer goldens. Reported/deferred glTF features remain owned by their L1-L6 diagnostics; the independent Khronos subset is docs/gltf-reference-comparison.json.

resolvedDivergences.symptom: An absent optional baseColorTexture sampled an unbound D3D11 SRV as transparent black, making factor-only PBR geometry invisible in transparent reference captures.
resolvedDivergences.resolution: The DirectX11 PBR binding now supplies the semantic opaque-white fallback for an absent base-colour map, guarded by both the cross-renderer source policy and a real DXVK pixel test.

resolvedDivergences.symptom: SkinnedEffect intentionally samples its texture even when none is assigned, and an unbound D3D11 SRV returned transparent black, erasing an otherwise valid untextured KHR_materials_unlit skin.
resolvedDivergences.resolution: The DirectX11 plain-skinned binding now substitutes the semantic opaque-white texture used by Vulkan, EasyGL and OpenGL, guarded by a source-policy regression and a real DXVK production-viewer capture that matches EasyGL byte-for-byte.

presentationRigExceptions.reason: The generic positive-octant camera sees the back of this deliberately non-planar morphed strip. Disabling culling makes its pixel path observable; dedicated culling fixtures retain culling coverage.
The generic positive-octant camera sees the back of the +X-rotated one-sided triangle. Disabling culling makes the transformed geometry observable without changing the fixture.

intentionalClearCaptures.reason: The fixture deliberately leaves one zero-weight vertex unweighted. Its zero skin matrix collapses that corner onto another corner, so the single triangle is degenerate and the clear framebuffer is the expected pixel result.
